release.note: Evidence record IDs name archived inputs, not live public URLs. Source and reproduction bundle await a clean release.

title: Recoverable radial halo memory has a tiny gravitational readout
finding: A selected spherical halo cohort passes radial echo controls in a prescribed background. A separate positive spatial model has a verified leading two-frequency prediction. Both unamplified force signals are small.
inference: The radial memory result supports this specified gravitational observable, while useful visible disk structure and self-consistent halo evolution remain untested.

units.normalization: Reference halo M0=1; all cohort weights remain absolute.
units.calibration: No astrophysical mass or length is fitted. A circular speed of 200 km/s is used only as an explicitly illustrative velocity conversion.

reference_background.energy_convention: E is positive binding energy, E=-E_orb; Phi0(infinity)=0.

force_fraction_reference.definition: Central-radius reference acceleration = vc(R=1)^2 / R, rather than an annular average.
force_fraction_reference.transformation: Square the recorded circular speed; R=1.

original_quadrupole_pilot.model: Two pure spatial m=2 quadrupole impulses with scales 0.8 and 1.6, orientations 0 and pi/4. These signed density redistributions were not guaranteed positive standalone sources.
original_quadrupole_pilot.sample: 8192 original QRNG/adaptive-subset records with eight deterministic azimuthal rotations each; they are not IID confidence units.
original_quadrupole_pilot.sampling_correction: Historical independent-block-standard-error labels were invalid. Corrected block spread is descriptive, not a confidence interval or detection significance.
original_quadrupole_pilot.interpretation: Underresolved late response. Physical azimuthal m and in-plane apsidal harmonic are distinct, so a planar same-m argument does not exclude its radial channels.

radial_cohort.initial_DF: Isotropic reference isochrone DF multiplied before forcing by a smooth binding-energy taper; zero at E<=0.02 and one at E>=0.04.
radial_cohort.selected_mass: Approximately 0.9521629 of the reference halo; no renormalization. The remaining halo response is untested.

impulses.source: Positive time-integrated Plummer mass; a_i has units M0 T0. A physical finite-duration history is not demonstrated.

observable.name: Mixed inward-negative radial acceleration
observable.readout: Actual Newtonian radial force averaged over log Rprime ~ Normal(log 1, 0.1^2).
observable.sign: Negative is inward; the signed mixed contrast may have either sign.
observable.memory_intervention: Average the post-A DF over radial angle at fixed new Jr,L and angular-momentum direction, preserving the new orbital-population marginal.
observable.statistical_uncertainty: Deterministic quadrature; no Monte Carlo confidence intervals. Numerical agreement is assessed against the mixed force.

figure.y_label: Mixed radial acceleration in G M0 / L0^2
figure.optional_display: Comparisons may use t-2tau or divide force by a_A a_B if the transformation is stated. The exported operands remain unscaled.

independent_formulation_curves.comparison: Independent forward and Eulerian trajectories on retained fixed dates
independent_formulation_curves.selection_predicate: 24 <= t <= 40; later 3 tau dates are excluded from the qualified interval.
independent_formulation_curves.metric_definition: Derived only from the two exported arrays on the stated retained dates.

positive_source_two_frequency.source_density: rho_I = rho_Plummer(M_I,s) [1 + epsilon (2x/(1+x^2))^l sin(theta)^l cos(l(phi-phi0))], x=r/s.
positive_source_two_frequency.source_potential: psi = -M_I/sqrt(r^2+s^2) - 3 M_I epsilon 2^l / ((2l+1)(2l+3)s) * x^l/(1+x^2)^(l+1/2) * sin(theta)^l cos(l(phi-phi0)).
positive_source_two_frequency.all_positive_sign_cases: Four epsilon-sign cases share the same two positive monopoles. The contrast [C++ - C+- - C-+ + C--]/4 isolates leading angular bilinear response.

declared_pair.coordinates: Canonical radial angle, apsidal angle, node; node frequency is zero.

positive_source_two_frequency.families: Radial-only, apsidal-only and genuine two-frequency channels are separate; nonrefocusing contributions are retained.
positive_source_two_frequency.observable: Equatorial l=m=2 Newtonian potential and actual annulus-averaged radial/tangential force coefficients at R=1, log width 0.1.
positive_source_two_frequency.normalization: Absolute reference-halo units for the same selected cohort; no cohort or pulse-amplitude renormalization. Curves are complex azimuthal coefficients, not already doubled physical fields.
positive_source_two_frequency.complex_convention: Physical field is C exp(2i phi) + conjugate. Potential/radial contrast is imaginary for the chosen orientations; tangential contrast is real.

positive_source_two_frequency.retained_temporal_failure: Sparse early times 2 and 4 missed a large initial transient; sparse late times also missed oscillations. Selected-node mean RMS was replaced by fixed-interval integration and cadence/action refinements.
positive_source_two_frequency.limitation: This is leading canonical mathematics. No finite-amplitude spatial echo, memory-erased spatial response, self-gravity or induced disk signal was measured.

limits: The radial result concerns a selected equilibrium cohort and the first 2 tau interval; later 3 tau and the unselected halo are not validated.
Fixed-background gravitational readouts do not establish self-consistent halo evolution, a live stellar disk, or a physical gas/encounter history.
The isolated linear stellar oscillator is not a stellar population. Its absolute-force bound applies to the specified interpolated field, not to a disk with self-gravitating amplification.
A real external perturbation acts directly on stars as well as on the halo; the halo-only pulses are diagnostic interventions.
No observations, Gaia origin, bar regeneration, or dark-matter discriminator have been validated.

primary_sources.title: Galactic echoes
primary_sources.role: Established galactic angle-action echo theory, stellar-slab examples and finite-amplitude behavior. The present controls replicate and extend its specified readouts, rather than introducing the basic mechanism.
